full_judgment:
2. The present petitioner Mst. Saleha Bibi was the pre-emptee and opposite party No. 1 Tayeb Ali Molla as pre-emptor filed an application under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The pre-emptor instituted the aforesaid miscellaneous case for pre-emption on the ground that the deed in question is an out and out sale deed and he being a co-sharer by inheritance was entitled to pre-empt the case land. This pre-emption application was opposed by the present petitioner Mst. Saleha Bibi being pre-emptee. It is her case that though it is a sale deed, in fact it is a deed of gift and by mistake the scribe had written it as a deed of sale instead of deed of gift. The pre-emptee examined five witnesses. The opposite party No. 1 pre-emptee examined six witnesses in this case. After considering the evidence on record the learned Munsif by his judgment dated 15.7.73 dismissed the application for pre-emption holding that it is a deed of gift. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and order of the pre-emptor preferred an appeal which was registered as Miscellaneous Appeal No. 23 of 1973. This Appeal was disposed of by the learned Additional District Judge, Bogra who after considering the materials on record and hearing the parties set aside the judgment and order of the learned Munsif and sent the case back on remand for reconsideration after adding a person as party in the case. Being aggrieved by the judgment and order dated 11.12.73 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Bogra in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 23 of 1973 the pre-emptee preferred this revisional application and obtained the present Rule. 

 5. Mr. Shahidul Islam submits that had it been so then the pre-emptee could have filed a suit under section 31 of the Specific Relief Act for correction of the deed, but it was not done. When this application under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act was filed for pre-emption at that time this new case was made by the pre-emptee-petitioner. If I read the evidence of P.Ws and O.P.Ws and Ext. A in juxtaposition with the provisions of Sections 91 and 92 of the Evidence Act. It clearly appears to me that this Ext. A is an out and out sale deed and by no manner of interpretation it can be treated as a deed of gift. The oral evidence as given by the O.P.Ws cannot alter or change the contents of the sale deed. Ex. 4. I have gone through the evidence of PWs and OPWs in this case. It appears to me that if I read the deed of sale along with the evidence of PWs 1 and 2, it will be clear that it is a deed of sale out and out. The D.Ws wanted to prove by saying that due to love and affection this property was given to the plaintiff by way of gift and not by way of sale. This oral evidence is contrary to the deed. Ext. A. which cannot be accepted in view of the provisions of Sections 91 and 92 of the Evidence Act. So, on the materials on record. It hold that this Ext. A is a deed of sale out and out and it cannot be treated as a deed of gift in any manner whatsoever. 

 8. In the result, this Rule is made absolute and the order of remand of the Lower Appellate Court is set aside and the order of the learned Munsif is also set aside and the application on the pre-emptor opposite party No. 1 under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act for pre-emption is hereby allowed. No cost.
